themes_detail.label: Curb Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints surged to 12 reports THIS WEEK, a 773% spike versus the 1.4-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.07), suggesting acute street infrastructure deterioration across Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 12 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 per-week 8-week average (773% increase)
Z-score of 8.07 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Coincides with street condition complaints up 368% last week (233 vs. 49.8 avg), suggesting interconnected street infrastructure crisis
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent snow/ice events or freeze-thaw cycles are triggering curb damage; verify if street maintenance crews are responding
Map the 12 complaints to identify if damage is concentrated in specific corridors (e.g., near transit, major intersections) that warrant prioritized repair

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 4 reports THIS WEEK, a 967% spike versus the 0.4-per-week baseline (z-score: 7.49), indicating possible new enforcement focus, permit violations, or resident friction over pandemic-era dining structures.
evidence: 4 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 per-week 8-week average (967% increase)
Z-score of 7.49 indicates highly anomalous spike
Active rezoning applications (21-31 46th Ave, 50-02 Queens Blvd) and land use changes may be triggering new commercial activity or enforcement
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department and DCLA to determine if new outdoor dining permits were issued or enforcement actions begun this week
Talk to local restaurant owners and residents to understand complaints: are they related to noise, obstruction, safety, or hygiene concerns?

themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints soared to 233 reports LAST WEEK, a 368% spike versus the 49.8-per-week baseline (z-score: 3.69), coinciding with winter weather and curb damage surge, indicating widespread pavement and pothole issues across the district.
evidence: 233 street condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 49.8 per-week 8-week average (368% increase)
Z-score of 3.69 indicates statistically significant spike
Clusters with curb damage spike (THIS WEEK) and illegal parking complaints (5,848 over 90 days), suggesting pot-filled streets may be exacerbating parking complaints
reporting_angles: Request Department of Transportation street inspection data for Sunnyside/Woodside; identify which streets/avenues have highest complaint density
Photograph deteriorated streets and interview residents about safety impacts, especially for seniors and cyclists on major corridors

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints jumped to 47 reports LAST WEEK, a 170% spike versus the 17.4-per-week baseline (z-score: 4.21), suggesting new construction, commercial activity, or enforcement pattern change affecting residential quality of life.
evidence: 47 noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 17.4 per-week 8-week average (170% increase)
Z-score of 4.21 indicates highly significant anomaly
647 building permits filed in last 90 days (437 alterations, 108 new buildings, 16 demolitions) suggest active construction contributing to noise source
reporting_angles: Cross-reference noise complaint addresses with DOB permit filings to identify which active construction projects are generating complaints
Interview residents and community board members about whether 24-hour construction, weekend work, or new commercial venues are driving complaints

themes_detail.label: Site Safety & Indoor Air Quality Concerns
themes_detail.summary: BEST/Site Safety complaints spiked to 3 reports 2 WEEKS AGO (2300% increase from 0.1 baseline, z-score: 8.69), and indoor air quality complaints jumped to 11 LAST WEEK (203% spike, z-score: 3.48), together suggesting potential construction safety or environmental hazards in the district.
evidence: Site safety complaints: 3 reports 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 per-week 8-week average (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Indoor air quality complaints: 11 reports LAST WEEK vs. 3.6 per-week 8-week average (203% increase, z-score: 3.48)
647 DOB permits filed in 90 days indicate construction activity; permits may lack adequate safety controls or dust mitigation
reporting_angles: Request DOB records for any 311 site safety complaints resolved 2 weeks ago; identify the project and construction company, verify compliance
Interview environmental health advocates and residents about indoor air quality; investigate whether construction dust, mold, or new commercial activity is the culprit
